page: Amazon Web Services r5b.xlarge is a memory-optimized fifth-generation instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the r5b.xlarge exhibits modest compute capabilities. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests for large blocks show read speeds of 26.41 GB/sec and write speeds of 22.94 GB/sec, which are categorized as weak. However, the instance maintains an average Passmark memory score of 2145.03, reflecting stable memory subsystem performance despite the lower CPU throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the r5b.xlarge is its high memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with relatively low processing power and baseline network speeds. This configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require a larger memory footprint but do not demand intensive CPU calculations. It is suitable for medium-sized database deployments, caching layers such as Redis, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that fit within a 32 GB memory envelope.
